name: Long-Term Solar Maintenance Expectations for LA County Homeowners

mainEntity.name: What are realistic maintenance needs and costs for residential solar systems in Los Angeles County over 25 years?
mainEntity.text: What are realistic maintenance needs and costs for residential solar systems in Los Angeles County over 25 years?

acceptedAnswer.text: Although solar panels are generally low maintenance, a 25-year system in Los Angeles County will not be completely hands-off. Dust, smog, and occasional ash from wildfires can build up on modules, especially in dry months, reducing output. Many homeowners plan for professional cleaning every 6–12 months, though some with safe access rinse panels themselves. Professional cleaning costs vary but can add up over decades. Electronics are the other key maintenance area. Inverters, optimizers, and microinverters typically have shorter lifespans than panels. You may need an inverter replacement once during a 25‑year period, often after 10–15 years, depending on brand and technology. Monitoring software should be checked regularly; sudden drops or offline alerts may signal wiring issues, tripped breakers, or component failures. Budget for occasional service calls, especially outside your workmanship warranty period. Ask your installer or manufacturer what typical out-of-warranty diagnostics and repair visits cost. Clarify whether your monitoring includes proactive alerts and who responds. Finally, keep trees trimmed to prevent increasing shade over time. By planning for cleaning, electronics replacement, and minor repairs, you protect your system’s long-term performance and avoid unpleasant surprises midway through its life.
acceptedAnswer.description: Residential solar in Los Angeles County needs periodic cleaning, monitoring checks, and occasional inverter or electronics replacement over 25 years. Homeowners should budget for cleaning every 6–12 months, possible inverter replacement after 10–15 years, and minor repair costs, even though panels themselves require little routine service.
